summary: Staggered Okta SCIM provisioning causes temporary missing groups claim, denying Model Lab role grants
description:
Issue summary:
Users requesting access to the internal Model Lab (model-experiment console) are intermittently denied role grants immediately after Okta-approved Access Requests. Okta shows the user in the target group, but the OIDC token delivered to the identity-proxy occasionally lacks the groups claim for ~5-20 minutes after approval.

Impact:
- Affected users receive 403 on first login attempt to Model Lab after approval.
- Manual re-login or waiting ~10 minutes results in correct access (groups claim arrives).
- Impacts internal workflows for PMs/engineers onboarding to Model Lab; non-blocking for production traffic but causes wasted time and support overhead.

Observed behavior:
- Access Request flow finishes in Redwood Console and Okta admin shows group membership updated.
- Identity-proxy logs for the auth callback show token without groups claim on the first exchange. Subsequent token refreshes contain groups.
- SCIM audit events show a staggered provisioning sequence: user profile created/updated followed by group membership patch delayed by Okta's internal queue for the SCIM connector.

Initial hypothesis:
SCIM connector returns group-membership updates out-of-order (or delayed) relative to the SAML/OIDC assertion issuance window. The auth stack accepts first token and enforces RBAC immediately, so the user is denied until groups are present on a new token issuance or after the SCIM event triggers a re-provisioning of the session.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Submit Model Lab access request for test user in Console (approver in Okta approves).
2) Immediately attempt to login to model-lab.redwood.internal using SSO within 1-2 minutes of approval.
3) Observe 403 with 'missing role' message in the UI.
4) Wait 10 minutes or force token refresh / re-login -> login succeeds with expected roles.

2026-03-12T14:05:12Z console ERROR: authorization denied for user aisha.patel@redwood.com - required role 'model-lab:editor' not found

investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 14:30 - Support triage: confirmed reproducible with synthetic user. Intermittent across multiple approvers and teams; appears timing dependent.
14:50 - Reproduced with capture: token returned by Okta on initial auth does not include groups claim; ID token received before SCIM group patch completed in Okta's backend.

15:20 - IAM engineer (Miguel) checked SCIM connector logs: connector processed profile update then scheduled group membership update in a separate job; observed average delay 30-120s under current load spikes.

15:45 - Identity-proxy currently treats first token as authoritative for session RBAC and does not trigger a background refresh on profile-change webhooks. No existing hook between SCIM patch completion and active session refresh for console flows.
16:10 - Hypothesis refined: race between IdP token issuance and eventual SCIM group write causes initial OIDC token to lack groups; system design assumes immediate group sync which is not guaranteed.
17:00 - Temporary mitigation tested: call to /auth/reauth endpoint after SCIM webhook (manual trigger) issues new token with groups and restores access.
comments: Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12T14:12: 'Customer reported: approved in Console but got 403 when trying to open Model Lab. User had to wait ~12 minutes.'

IAM (Miguel) 2026-03-12T15:25: 'I see SCIM connector is batching group patches. Will dig into connector config and Okta rate-limits. Possible fix: reduce batching or emit immediate group-change webhook.'

SRE (Olivia Chen) 2026-03-12T16:00: 'Identity-proxy should probably accept a 'pending_grouplookup' mode: allow session creation with limited access and request on-demand token refresh when group claim appears. Short-term workaround: instruct approvers to trigger 'force re-provision' for user or ask user to re-login.'

Platform Eng (Samir Rao) 2026-03-13T09:10: 'Raised PR to add a background token refresh on SCIM webhook for console paths (draft: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/421). Need to validate race conditions and ensure it doesn't open an access escalation window.'
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-14T08:05: 'Workaround documented in runbook; engineering to schedule a follow-up to implement safe refresh + telemetry. Marking In Progress.'
resolution: Workaround: added temporary guidance to Support runbook to instruct affected users to re-login if denied; operators can trigger immediate SCIM sync via admin tool. Engineering action items: (1) short-term: identity-proxy PR to listen for SCIM completion webhook and trigger a background token refresh for active sessions on console endpoints (PR #421 in review), (2) medium-term: change SCIM connector to emit group membership change as atomic event or reduce batching window, (3) add telemetry to alert when initial token lacks expected groups. Plan schedule: deploy identity-proxy change to staging 2026-03-18, canary to prod 2026-03-22 pending security review.
